blockers.issue: Too few comparable live samples to support the provisional distribution targets: 3 direct positive requests and 1 browser click-to-first-response request.
blockers.detail: More independent real-GPT runs on the reviewed code and approved isolated environment are needed. The samples show observed latency, not median or p95 product performance.

blockers.issue: No resource telemetry for the complete GPT+n8n+browser workload.
blockers.detail: Available host-wide samples were partial, not process-isolated, and do not report a complete run's CPU, memory, and swap envelope.

blockers.issue: FastEmbed evidence covers offline reloads and a 250-note synthetic index rebuild, not the complete product path or larger index workload.
blockers.detail: The isolated measurements are useful and do not show a defect. They cannot establish request percentiles or safe scaling to larger vaults.

1_performance_verdict.scope: This is a Performance verdict only. It does not claim that the full four-specialist audit passes.

2_threshold_status.twenty_plus_twenty: Self-authored provisional experimental sample target in the v9 preflight, not a user-approved hard feature requirement or SLA/SLO.
2_threshold_status.performance_signoff: The role instructions require measured performance and relevant resource evidence; they do not prescribe 20+20. A bounded independent review can report observed results and their limits without claiming statistical certification.
2_threshold_status.future_product_slo_certification: Requires an explicitly approved user-facing SLO, workload, and sampling method. Do not present the provisional 60s/90s medians or 120s p95 targets as accepted product commitments.
2_threshold_status.defect_handling: Do not waive a reproducible regression or unsafe resource behavior merely because the numerical thresholds were provisional.

3_minimum_next_test_plan.purpose: Obtain useful evidence for an independent performance review without claiming an invented p95 or treating a self-imposed sample count as product policy.
method: Freeze and identify the exact reviewed commit and test configuration; use only disposable synthetic data and the Pi ARM64 4 GiB + 2 GiB swap environment.

Run a small, predeclared set of at least 3 independent successful direct requests and 3 independent authenticated browser+n8n+GPT requests, with distinct valid source examples. Record safe abstentions and failures separately; do not count them as positive latency samples.
Measure direct request wall time and browser click-to-first-response with monotonic clocks. Record full harness duration separately and never mix it into user-response latency.

For every run, capture host MemAvailable, SwapFree, CPU load/utilization if available, temperature, and process/container RSS; sample throughout the complete workload at a fixed interval. Record concurrency and whether caches/model are warm or cold.

Report each observation, sample count, median only where the sample supports a descriptive median, and min/max. Label p95 unavailable at this sample size. Report FastEmbed load/query and index rebuild as separate offline measurements with cache state, note count, and peak RSS.
Compare with an earlier run only if workload, timing boundary, code-path, and environment are comparable; investigate any repeatable material slowdown or resource exhaustion before signoff.
3_minimum_next_test_plan.not_claimed: This minimum plan is a bounded evidence review, not an SLO certification or a statistically reliable p95 estimate.

mismatched_boundaries: The v11 browser receipt's 42.29 seconds is click-to-first-response; 86.19 seconds is the full harness including setup and replay. They are distinct metrics and must not be pooled.
The v10 browser 110.45 seconds is a historical full-harness duration without the v11 interaction timer, so it is not comparable to click-to-first-response.
Direct request durations and browser click-to-first-response have different boundaries; report separately.
The 971 MiB MemAvailable figure is from a prior partial host sample; the v10 JSON has a later partial minimum of 993984 KiB. Neither is isolated product RSS or complete-run telemetry.
FastEmbed's 1.04 GiB peak RSS and 250-note rebuild times describe an isolated synthetic indexing workload, not end-to-end GPT request latency.
4_boundaries_and_regressions.evidence: The three current direct positives completed in 37.823, 38.767, and 50.135 seconds; the browser request completed in 42.29 seconds. The supplied evidence demonstrates insufficient coverage for distributional/resource signoff, not a measured regression. The full four-specialist feature audit remains unclaimed.

review_type: independent precheck, not the four-specialist feature acceptance
